transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because I’ve been feeling really wound up most of the day. It’s like my body is bracing for something, even when I’m just sitting at my computer or trying to relax after dinner.
Have you been feeling anxious or fearful about anything in particular?

Not one single thing, really. It jumps around. I’ll start worrying about my sister in Arecibo, then whether I missed something at work, then my husband driving home, or church things I said I’d help with, or bills. I catch myself planning for problems that haven’t even happened yet.
Have you experienced any episodes where you felt an intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get anxious and tense, but I haven’t noticed it coming on suddenly like that or peaking within a few minutes.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and are difficult to control?

Yes. It’s like I’ll tell myself, “Daniela, enough, focus on this report,” but then one small worry turns into five more. Before I know it, I’ve spent half an hour checking messages or going over what could go wrong.
Do you feel compelled to perform specific rituals or behaviors to reduce your anxiety?
Not really. I mean, I might check my phone or go over things in my head, but I don’t have a specific ritual I feel I have to do to make the anxiety go away.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations or activities because of your anxiety?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I avoid whole situations because of it. Sometimes I put things off a bit if I’m feeling anxious, but I still usually do what I need to do.
Do you have thoughts that are intrusive or unwanted, and that you try to suppress or ignore?

Yes, I do get thoughts I don’t really want, and I try to push them aside. Like I’ll tell myself, okay Daniela, stop, focus on the report. But then that one worry turns into several, and I end up spending a lot of time checking messages or replaying what might go wrong.
Do you have any recurring thoughts or images that you consider irrational or senseless?

I don’t think so. I mean, I have worries that come back a lot, but I wouldn’t say they’re images or thoughts that feel senseless or irrational in that way. They usually feel like regular worries, just hard to let go of.
Do you often feel restless or on edge, like you can't relax?
Yes. That’s actually a big part of why I came in. I feel wound up almost all day, like my body is bracing for something, even when I’m just sitting at my computer or trying to relax after dinner.
Do you have thoughts that are recurring and difficult to control, which are not just worries about everyday things?
Not really, no. They’re mostly everyday worries that get stuck, like work or family things. I don’t have a separate kind of recurring thought that feels different from that.
Would you say your anxiety is mostly about a few specific things or is it more general, covering many different aspects of your life?

It’s more general. My mind kind of jumps from one thing to the next—my sister in Arecibo, whether I missed something at work, my husband driving home, church responsibilities, bills. I end up planning for problems that haven’t even happened.
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that seemed to come out of nowhere?
I don’t think so. I get anxious and tense, but it doesn’t really hit me suddenly out of nowhere like that.
Have you ever had a period of intense fear or discomfort that seemed to peak within a few minutes?
No, I can’t think of a time like that. I get worked up sometimes, but it doesn’t really peak suddenly within a few minutes.
Has your anxiety been interfering with your ability to do daily tasks or enjoy activities you normally like?

A little, yes. I’m still getting things done—I go to work, I’m there for my family, and I keep up with church—but it takes more effort. Reports take me longer because I keep checking them, and I’ve noticed I can sound short with people I care about, so I’ve had to apologize for that.
How long have you been feeling this general anxiety that jumps from one thing to another?
It’s been about thirteen months now. I think it really started when my sister in Arecibo began needing a lot more help from the family.
Do you have any thoughts that you try to ignore or get rid of, but they keep coming back to you?

Yes. I’ll try to push the thoughts away and tell myself, “Daniela, enough, focus on this report,” but then one worry turns into five more. Before I know it, I’ve spent half an hour checking messages or going over what could go wrong.
Do you have thoughts that are repetitive, intrusive, and difficult to control, which are not just about everyday worries?
I don’t think so. The thoughts feel repetitive, but they’re usually about regular things—family, work, what I need to handle. I wouldn’t say they’re strange or separate from everyday worries.
Do you have thoughts that are not just worries about everyday things, but rather repetitive and intrusive thoughts that are difficult to control?
Not really, no. I mean, the thoughts repeat, but they’re about normal life things. I haven’t noticed any other kind of intrusive thought beyond that.
Have you been feeling this way of being wound up and anxious for most days over the past 6 months?
Yes, most days. It’s been going on for about thirteen months now, since my sister in Arecibo started needing a lot more help from the family.
Has your anxiety been present for more days than not over the past six months?
Yes. It’s been more days than not, for sure. It’s been going on around thirteen months now, since my sister in Arecibo started needing a lot more help from the family.
